title: When Things Fall Apart

canonicalEdition.name: First edition
canonicalEdition.sourceProvenance: Frozen web bundle only: bibliographic records, table-of-contents evidence, official publication metadata, and narrow secondary summary support. Paraphrase-first; no full text frozen.

anchorSummary: This chapter is the book's core CEO playbook for collapse conditions, turning suffering into action on communication, layoffs, executive judgment, and the refusal to hide from the truth.
coreClaim: When the company is breaking, the CEO earns the role by facing ugly reality directly and making painful people decisions without false comfort or performative softness.
distinctMechanism: Horowitz bundles specific crisis-management situations into one operating doctrine: tell it like it is, execute layoffs cleanly, fire or demote decisively when needed, and stop expecting anyone to rescue you.
requiredAnchors: The struggle: the private psychological burden of knowing the company can fail on your watch.
Tell it like it is: truthful communication matters more in fear than polished reassurance.
Layoffs and executive decisions: hard people calls must be made clearly, quickly, and without self-protective delay.
specificApplications: Use direct communication to stabilize a frightened team.
Design layoffs and executive transitions around clarity, speed, and respect.
Treat the struggle as a leadership burden to metabolize, not a reason to freeze.
commonMisreadings: Reducing the chapter to macho suffering instead of disciplined truth and responsibility.
Treating tough people decisions as cruelty rather than clarity about the company's needs.
hardEdgeRequirement: Hard mode must show why delaying painful decisions to feel kinder often increases the damage for everyone involved.
thresholdQuestion: What obligations remain when every available option harms someone and the leader still has to choose?
